editorial.headline: Defence Institutions: A Closed Investment Activity
editorial.standfirst: A defence-and-armed-forces institutional activity closed to foreign investment nationally and in Bali, despite Bali’s risk note placing it outside the province-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 84221 concerns the institutional work of defence and armed forces. Its scope is deliberately broad: administration, operations and other activities are all within it. The record also includes civilian employees working within the military environment and undertakings that deliver aid to military members. At the same time, it separates the institution’s functions from individual armed-forces members who are employed or who hold government office. Government defence bodies and the Headquarters of the Indonesian National Armed Forces are the examples given for the institutional terrain in view.

The relevant actor is therefore the defence or armed-forces institution carrying out those functions, not a generic private-business proposition. The record lists no business scale as open to the activity. That is an operational fact rather than a missing detail: the slim record provides no scale-based route into this code. For a founder examining registration options, the category has to be read on its defined institutional terms, including its civilian-staffing and military-member aid functions.

Nationally, the investment position is unequivocal. The PMA status is closed, and the maximum foreign ownership is 0%. No foreign stake can be registered in this activity. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. These details do not create a partial foreign-ownership threshold or a conditional opening; the record classifies the activity as closed to PMA at the national level.

Bali closes it as well. A foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today: the Bali record marks it closed and blocked. One detail requires careful reading. The activity is noted as medium-high/high risk and is stated not to be blocked by Bali’s province-wide moratorium, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on a permanent, island-wide basis. The note also calls for verification by address. The absence of a moratorium block is not an opening: both the national and Bali positions are closed to PMA.
